label: Romney Runs as Independent Candidate
detail: Mitt Romney, the former Republican nominee and Utah senator, appears on the ballot as an independent candidate, drawing moderate and anti-incumbent-party voters.
assumption: The request to make him the nominee of the party that has held the White House since 2021 is not possible in this framework, which fixes both major nominees; it is modelled as a Romney independent bid. He draws voters from both nominees, mostly moderate and college-educated Republicans and independents.
facts_text: A former governor and one-time presidential nominee who now sits in the Senate has qualified for the ballot in most states as an independent candidate.
He has said he will campaign as a moderate alternative to both major-party nominees.

candidate.name: Mitt Romney
candidate.descriptor: Former Massachusetts governor, former presidential nominee and retired U.S. senator from Utah
positions: Has called for reducing the federal deficit and reforming entitlement programs.
Has supported a strong U.S. role in alliances and backing for Ukraine.
Has voted to convict the former president in both impeachment trials and criticized his character.

research_questions: How did voters behave when a prominent moderate ran as an independent, as with John Anderson in 1980?
How much did independent candidates draw from each major party's voters in past elections?
Did centrist third-party bids change turnout among moderate and college-educated voters?
source_text: mit romney runs against donald trump as the democratic nominee instead of kamala harris
